paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Three days without water, and the people grumble, and later with empty stomachs they grumble again (Exodus 15:24; 16:2). But look who answers every time: the LORD sweetens the bitter water, says "I am the LORD who heals you" (Exodus 15:26), and rains down bread from heaven (Exodus 16:4). Moses even tells them their grumbling was "not against us but against the LORD" (Exodus 16:8), and the LORD still heard it (Exodus 16:12).

The bread comes with a lesson in trusting Him: gather enough for that day, and He says this is how He will test whether they follow His instructions (Exodus 16:4). Some people kept leftovers anyway (Exodus 16:20), and I get it, friend, because I've watched a timer and still pulled the batch early. But on the sixth day He gave them enough for two days, so they could rest on the Sabbath (Exodus 16:29).

So what does that mean for you, baker? When you're in the desert, whether it's a bill, a long week or a plan that fell through, the LORD can take care of you one day at a time. Bring your needs to Him instead of grumbling, the way Moses cried out to the LORD at Marah (Exodus 15:25). And Aaron put a jar of manna before the LORD, "to be preserved for the generations to come" (Exodus 16:33), so they could see the bread He fed them (Exodus 16:32).
